To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Tir 1 was mapped to a 0.7 cM region on chromosome 17; Tir 2 to a 0,5 cM region on mouse chromosome 5; and Tir 3 to three intervals on mouse chromosome 1, namely Tir 3a to a 6 cM region, Tir 3c to a 2 cM region and Tir 3b to a 7.2 cM region.
we have identified the genes conferring susceptibility to trypanosomiasis in mice.
the major trypanosomiasis resistance locus Tir1 has been fine mapped to a 1.2 cM interval and two minor loci, Tir2 and Tir4, have been mapped to 1.1 cM and 1.2-2.2 cMb, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mouse models to identify trypanotolerance genes, and this is a step towards the identification of the trypanotolerance candidate genes.
identifying the trypanotolerance gene(s) in mouse models, and this is an essential first step towards identifying the genes in trypanotolerent cattle breeds.
fine mapping of trypanotolerance loci in mice, which is a prerequisite for identification of genes underlying the QTL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genes underlying Tir 2 and three Tir 3 loci are within 2.2-7.2 cM intervals on MMU5 and MMU1 respectively.
trypanosomotic resistance in mice is conferred by three major QTL, namely Tir 1, 2 and 3.
the genes underlying Tir 1, 2 and 3 have been fine mapped and the QTL regions are now ready to be mined for candidate genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trypanotolerance gene effect of Tir1 is additive, and the gene effect of the Tir1 is 2.5 times higher than the combined effects of Tir2 and Tir 2.
Tir 2 and three intervals of Tir 3 have been fine mapped and the genes within these intervals can be investigated for their potential role in trypanotolerance in cattle and mice.

Tir 1 is the major QTL and Tir 2 is the minor QTL for trypanotolerence, and that the Tir 3 locus may be composed of three distinct QTL, Tir 3a and 3c for trypanotolernce and Tir 3b for trypanosusceptiblity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the F12 A/J × C57BL/ 6J AIL population is a useful genetic resource to fine map QTLs and identify candidate genes underlying trypanotolerance in mice.
high resolution mapping in AIL populations can be successfully used to map trypanotolerance loci in mouse models.
fine mapping in the mouse model can be a powerful approach for the identification of genes underlying trypanotolerance.
